questions.question: Who is known as the father of Green Revolution in the World?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Norman Borlaug.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Norman Borlaug** is known as the **father of Green Revolution** in the World.
 
• He was an** American agronomist** and **humanitarian **who is credited with saving over a billion people from starvation.
 
• Borlaug developed **high-yielding disease-resistant wheat varieties** that helped increase food production in developing countries.
 
• He received the **Nobel Peace Prize in 1970** for his contributions to world peace through increasing food supply.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **R. K. V. Rao** was an **Indian economist and statistician** who made significant contributions to the field of economics.

 
 
• The VKRV Rao Prizes in **Social Science Research **are given in his honor.
 
 
 
• **M. S. Swaminathan** is an Indian** geneticist and agronomist** who is known for his role in India's Green Revolution.
 
 
• He is referred to as "**the Father of Economic Ecology"** by the United Nations Environment Programme.

questions.question: What is the trophic level of dead organic matter in detritus food chain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**first.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **detritus food chain** starts with the **dead organic matter, **which is then consumed by detritivores such as **earthworms, snails, and bacteria.**
 
• The dead organic matter is also known as** detritus,** and it is the** primary source of energy** for the detritus food chain.
 
• Since the dead organic matter is the** initial source of energy,** it is considered to be at the first trophic level.
 
• The detritus food chain is important as it helps in the** recycling of nutrients** in the ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** fourth trophic level** refers to the **tertiary consumers**, which are organisms that feed on the** secondary consumers**.

 
 
• These are usually **top predators** in the food chain.
 
 
 
• The **second trophic level **refers to the primary consumers, which are **herbivores.**
 
 
• They feed on **producers.**
 
 
 
• The** third trophic level **refers to the secondary consumers, which are **carnivores.**
 
 
• They feed on the** primary consumers.**

questions.question: Which scheme was launched in the rural areas of the country to bring every assisted family above the poverty line within three years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana** was launched in **1999 **to provide** self-employment opportunities** to** rural poor** and bring assisted families **above the poverty line** within **three years.**
 
• This Yojana is a program that is implemented by **commercial banks, cooperative banks, and regional banks **and is overseen by the **federal government **and **state governments **in a** 75:25** ratio.
 
• As the name implies, the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana primarily targets **low-income households** or groups - referred to as **"Swarrozgars"** in the local vernacular.
 
• It aims to generate** revenue and jobs** in order to assist people in rising **beyond the poverty line.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gramin Udyami Yojana is** also known as** Rural Entrepreneurship Development Programme.**

 
 
• It was launched in **1995** to provide **self-employment** opportunities to** rural artisans** and** unemployed youth.**
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana** was launched in **1993.**
 
 
• It aimed to provide employment opportunities to the **urban and rural unemployed youth.**
 
 
 
• **Garib Kalyan Rozgar Yojana** was launched in **2020.**
 
 
• It aimed to provide employment opportunities to** migrant workers** who returned to their home states during the COVID-19 pandemic.

questions.question: In which areas is intensive subsistence agriculture practiced?

options.text: area without population pressure on land
Areas with average population pressure on land
Areas with low population pressure on land
areas with high population pressure on land

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**areas with high population pressure.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gahana Nirvah Krishi** refers to intensive agriculture, where farmers use **advanced techniques **and **high-quality inputs** to maximize yields from a limited area of land.
 
• It is common in the densely inhabited monsoon regions of **southeast, east, and south Asia.**
 
• In areas with** high population pressure**, farmers practice intensive agriculture to produce **more food from limited land resources** to meet the increasing demand for food.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In areas with** low population pressure**, farmers have more land available, and they can practice** extensive agriculture,** which focuses on producing more food by cultivating a larger area of land.
 
• In areas with** average population pressure**, farmers practice **semi-intensive agriculture,** which is a mix of intensive and extensive agriculture techniques.
 
• In areas with** no population pressure**, farmers may not practice agriculture at all, or they may practice **subsistence agriculture,** which is focused on producing enough food for their own consumption.

questions.question: What type of governance structure was proposed in the draft National Air Sports Policy (NASP) by the Ministry of Civil Aviation in January 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**two-tier.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Civil Aviation **proposed a **two-tiered governance **structure for the **National Air Sports Policy **(NASP) draft in **January 2022.**
 
• The two-tiered governance structure comprises of a **National Air Sports Council** (NASC) and a **National Air Sports Management Committee (NASMC).**
 
• The NASC will be the apex body responsible for **policy formulation** and overall guidance, whereas the NASMC will be responsible for **implementation and monitoring** of the policy.
 
• The NASP aims to promote **air sports** in India and provide a framework for the development of air sports infrastructure,** training, and safety** measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **National Air Sports Policy** (NASP) is a policy framework proposed by the** Ministry of Civil Aviation** to promote air sports in India.
 
• The goal outlined in NASP 2022 is to position India by **2030** as one of the world's leading sports nations.
 
• The National Air Sports Council (NASC) will have representatives from various** ministries, regulatory bodies, and industry stakeholders**, while the National Air Sports Management Committee (NASMC) will have **representatives from the NASC **and other relevant **stakeholders.**

questions.question: Choose among the given options, the function of the budget is:

options.text: to provide detailed description of incomes and expenditure of Government
to provide description of states and union

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**to provide detailed description of incomes and expenditure of Government.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** function **of the budget is to:

 
 
• **Allocate resources:** The budget provides a plan for allocating resources to different sectors and programs based on their **priorities and needs**.
 
• **Control spending: **The budget helps in controlling spending by **setting limits on the amount of money** that can be spent on different programs and activities.
 
• **Monitor performance:** The budget provides a framework for **monitoring** the performance of different programs and activities to ensure that they are meeting their objectives and delivering results.
 
• **Communicate priorities:** The budget communicates the government's **priorities and policies **to the public and other stakeholders, helping to build trust and support for the government's actions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **budget** is a **financial plan** that outlines the expected** revenues and expenditures** for a specific period, usually one year.
 
• The main purpose of a budget is to** allocate resources and control spending** to achieve specific goals and objectives.
 
• A budget may include revenues from **taxes, fees, and other sources**, as well as expenditures on programs, services, and infrastructure.
 
• The budget process typically involves** setting priorities, negotiating **with stakeholders, and making **trade-offs** between competing demands for resources.
 
• The budget is an essential tool for **governments, businesses, and individuals** to manage their finances and achieve their goals.

questions.question: Kathakali primarily originated from which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a traditional **dance-drama **form that originated in the state of **Kerala** in southwestern India.
 
• It is believed to have developed in the **17th century, **and combines elements of **dance, drama, music, and ritual.**
 
• The word "Kathakali" comes from two Malayalam words: **"katha" (story) and "kali" (performance)**.
 
• The elaborate costumes, makeup, and facial expressions used in Kathakali performances are distinctive and help to convey the** emotions and characters** of the story being told.
 
• Kathakali has become popular not just in Kerala but also in other parts of India and around the world, as a **unique and captivating** form of theatrical art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karnataka** is a neighboring state of **Kerala**, and has its own rich tradition of classical dance forms such as **Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi.**
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**, located further to the east, is known for its own dance forms such as **Kuchipudi and Vilasini Natyam.**
 
• **Tamil Nadu**, located to the east of Kerala, is known for its own classical dance forms such as **Bharatanatyam and Mohiniyattam.**
 
 
• There is a similar dance-drama form called "**Therukoothu**" that is popular in Tamil Nadu and shares some similarities with Kathakali.

questions.question: In post-independent India, the first elected Parliament came into existence in ________.

__
 
• The **first general elections** in independent India were held in **1951-52.**
 
• The **first elected Parliament** came into existence on **April 17, 1952.**
 
• The Parliament consisted of two houses - the **Council of States** (Rajya Sabha) and the **House of the People** (Lok Sabha).
 
• The Constitution of India came into force on **January 26, 1950**, but the first Parliament was formed only after the general elections were held in 1951-52.

• The 1st Lok Sabha was** dissolved **on** April 4, 1957**, having served its whole five-year term.
 
• On **May 13, 1952**, the First Session of this Lok Sabha convened.

questions.question: Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with _________.

options.text: Distribution of power between centre and states

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distribution of power between centre and states.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains three lists, namely **Union List, State List, and Concurrent List,** which specify the subjects and areas of governance that are under the jurisdiction of the **central government, state governments**, and both central and state governments, respectively.
 
• The distribution of power between the centre and the states is one of the** key features** of the Indian federal system.
 
• The Constitution defines the scope and limits of the legislative and executive powers of both the central and state governments, and also provides for mechanisms to **resolve disputes** between them.
 
• The Seventh Schedule is an important tool for maintaining the **balance of power **between the centre and the states, and for ensuring that both have their respective roles and responsibilities in the governance of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​The Indian Constitution consists of **12 Schedules**.

 
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935,** which contained 10 Schedules, was one of the earliest documents to mention schedules.
 
• **Eight Schedules **made up the Indian Constitution when it was eventually enacted in **1949.**
 
• **Additional provisions** that give comprehensive information on different parts of the Indian Constitution are found in the Schedules.
 
 
 
• **Powers of Parliament** are specified in **Articles 245 to 255**.
 
• The **Panchayat Raj system** is governed by the provisions of** Part IX** of the Constitution.
 
• The **judiciary of the states **is governed by the provisions of **Part VI **of the Constitution.

questions.question: What kind of weather conditions are experienced as the distance from sea increases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Extreme.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **distance from the sea** affects the **weather** conditions in a significant way. 
 
• The **farther away** from the sea, the **more extreme** the weather conditions become.
 
• When the distance from the sea** increases**, there is a** decrease **in the **moderating effect of the sea** on the climate, which results in extreme weather conditions.
 
• Extreme weather conditions can include **high temperatures, low temperatures, heavy precipitation**, and **strong winds.**
 
• The distance from the sea also affects the **humidity levels**, with inland areas experiencing lower humidity levels than coastal areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Light weather conditions **can be experienced in areas** closer to the sea**, where the moderating effect of the sea on the climate is stronger.

 
 
• Light weather conditions can include** mild temperatures, light precipitation, and gentle winds.**
 
 
 
• **Moderate **weather conditions can be experienced in areas that are** moderately far** from the sea.
 
 
• These areas may experience** moderate temperatures, moderate precipitation, and moderate winds**.
 
 
 
• The term** temperate **refers to a specific type of climate that is characterized by mild temperatures and moderate precipitation.
 
 
• Temperate climates are typically found in **areas closer to the sea,** where the moderating effect of the sea on the climate is stronger.
